thread.title: Stocks Jump On Tame Inflation Data As These 2 Chip Names Soar

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Jump On Tame Inflation Data As These 2 Chip Names Soar
text:
Stocks opened to solid gains Tuesday as chip stocks boosted early trade, along with added lift from healthy February inflation data.
X The   average pulsed 0.4% higher at the starting bell, boosted by Intel ( INTC ), but held back by General Electric's ( GE ) early 3% dive. The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.5%, despite Qualcomm's ( QCOM ) 5% decline at the open. The S&P 500 jumped 0.4%.
Overseas action was mild on Tuesday, though in the U.S., politics was all over the premarket session. Qualcomm dived after President Trump late Monday ordered the attempted hostile takeover of the chipmaker by Singapore-based Broadcom ( AVGO ) blocked due to national security concerns . Investors were also monitoring banking and financial issues, after the Senate late Monday approved amendments to proposed rollbacks to Dodd-Frank oversight rules , setting up the underlying bill for final approval later this week.
Early economic news was positive , with the Labor Department reporting its Consumer Price Index rose 0.2% in February. That was down from January's 0.5% surge, and in line with consensus projections. Core prices, minus energy and food, were also up 0.2% and in line with expectations, and down from a 0.3% gain in January.
Intel, Micron Lead Chip Gains; GE Dividend Labeled 'High Risk' Other than Qualcomm, chip stocks were in generally good shape , with Micron Technology ( MU ) up 5% and leading the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index as the stock looks to add to its powerful 9% advance from Monday.
Intel punched up nearly 2% to the top of the Dow as investors responded to the blocked Broadcom/Qualcomm deal. Intel was reported late last week to be considering its own bid for Broadcom, in order to avert a competitive threat . A four-week advance drove Intel shares to a new high Friday. The stock traded just below that high on Monday, and up 12% since the start of the year.

Also on the Dow, General Electric tumbled 3% lower after JPMorgan cut the stock's price target to 11, from 14. The note cited "structural concerns in the key power markets, minimal margin for error on leverage," and a free-cash flow/dividend ratio that puts the company's already lowered payout at "high risk."
Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and Netflix ( NFLX ) led the FANG stock tech leaders , up more than 1% apiece. Apple ( AAPL ) rose 0.6%. Google parent Alphabet ( GOOGL ) gained 1%, and will remain under the microscope this week, as it hovers just below a 1,197.10 buy point in a six-week cup base .
Retail names were sharply mixed in early action. Tilly's ( TLYS ) dropped 15% after delivering weak fourth-quarter results late Monday. DSW ( DSW ) popped 7%, after raising its quarterly dividend, and despite reporting a broad fourth-quarter earnings miss.
Trump Ousts Tillerson, European Stocks Dive, China Mixed Markets generally showed little response to the breaking news that President Trump had fired Secretary of State Rex Tillerson and swapped CIA Director Mike Pompeo into the job. But Europe's markets — which had gained following U.S. inflation data —weakened on the news, with London's FTSE 100 and Frankfurt's DAX both losing ground in afternoon trade. China-based stocks, which had logged a positive premarket session, turned lower in early trade.
Many China-based stocks gave up premarket advances and traded lower, though not necessarily due to the State Department news.
One clear exception, Jupai HoldingsJP, leapt 5% in early trade after reporting Q4 results late Thursday. Shares are climbing the right side of a cup[ base with a 24.52 buy point.
